The qwen model's initial PKGBUILD audit actually found it safe ('No executable code in global scope; safe to parse'), but then failed during the full review phase. The deepseek model successfully reviewed all three files (PKGBUILD, .SRCINFO, .gitignore) and found them safe: standard Rust project packaging with pinned source (v1.11.2 tag), SHA256 checksum verification, no suspicious network operations, no obfuscated code, and no executable logic outside build/package functions. data.disagreement_analysis: The qwen model experienced an API failure (HTTP 400 BadRequestError) during the full PKGBUILD review phase, resulting in an inconclusive verdict. The qwen model's initial PKGBUILD audit (before the error) also found the file safe.

learnings: Tool errors (API failures, timeouts) should be clearly distinguished from security findings in the verdict logic - a failed audit should not trigger escalation when another model successfully completed the same review
